## Short answer

### Build-start priority — 3 October 2026

We should now prioritize external component evidence and workshop quotations over more generic study branches. There are **three release gates before full-tower construction**, not a requirement to finish outdoor/network research first: exact requirements/components, mechanical release, electrical release. Outdoor development follows the indoor prototype; it must not silently delay or be claimed by the indoor build.

**Time planning allowance, not a confirmed estimate:** reserve roughly **4–8 weeks from receipt of usable OEM information and availability of qualified services/parts** for a first safely commissioned indoor prototype and initial measurements. Illustrative allocation: 1–2 weeks for component-specific design/review, 2–4 weeks for fabrication/assembly/commissioning, and 1–2 weeks for initial indoor measurements. These are planning placeholders chosen for coordination, NOT quoted turnaround or a commitment by the assistant/workshop. They exclude unknown supplier-response/procurement delays, major redesign and outdoor validation. Reviews/tests can uncover rework; repeated validation may take longer. No start or completion date is booked.

| Start priority | Use the existing package | Exit evidence / who acts |
|---|---|---|
| A — component information and quotes | [Fan selection brief](FAN_SELECTION_BRIEF_R00.md), [filter supplier questions](SUPPLIER_RELEASE_QUESTIONS.md) | Exact supported fan/filter proposals, matched curves/manuals/drawings/masses, quotes and lead times; supplier replies obtained by authorized team contact |
| B — actual place and acceptance targets | [No-lab route](NO_LAB_BUILD_ROUTE.md), [funded scopes W02–W04](FUNDED_WORK_PACKAGES.csv) | Indoor premises/room dimensions, supply/site facts, accepted flow/noise and available qualified review/workshop scope; user/team confirms |
| C — fabrication-ready core | Existing CAD studies, [closure package](M05_CLOSURE_REVIEW_PACKAGE.md), [electrical sequence](CORE_CONTROL_SEQUENCE.md) | Assistant produces component-specific assembly/support/seal/base/guard and electrical drafts; qualified review resolves issues and releases scope |
| D — authorized build and test | Work packages W03–W08 | User authorizes released orders/services; workshop assembles; competent inspection/commissioning and actual data recorded |

A and B can proceed in parallel. C uses their verified inputs; D must not bypass C. Supplier requests are prepared but NOT SENT; no reviewer/workshop booked and no parts ordered. The current fan comparison still lacks confirmed loaded-duty capability. A new assumed fan envelope cannot close this dependency.

What may start earlier with a separate suitable scope: quotation discussions, workshop design/manufacturability review, non-operating packaging mock-ups and isolated low-voltage instrument setup. Do not cut final structural/pressure-boundary parts, improvise mains wiring or energize an unreviewed fan/filter assembly from current study files. Separate component-only work needs its own appropriate safety/release scope.

Immediate next real-world action: obtain **fan/filter selection responses and a combined review/fabrication/commissioning quote**, while confirming the indoor premises. The assistant continues preparing/revising drawings and calculations; the optional ENTC friend is not a prerequisite. More presentation software, solar, carbon research and a decorative cylinder are not the current critical path. Keep necessary guards, enclosure, seals and supports in the core.

Current delivery basis: funding only from college/NGO; no college lab dependency. Assistant prepares digital design; ENTC reviewer optional/unconfirmed. Obtain required qualified physical services commercially. See [no-lab execution plan](NO_LAB_BUILD_ROUTE.md).

We are in **design development**. The idea, initial CAD, screening calculations and functional plans exist. We are NOT yet ready to send final drawings for fabrication. No complete physical prototype has been built or tested.

There are **six major gates still open**. They overlap in effort; they are not six equal-sized tasks. Gates 1–3 must be closed before releasing the complete tower for fabrication/assembly. A controlled component-only bench test may have a separate reviewed scope, but is not authorized by this checklist.

| Gate | Already available | Still required to close it | Who/input needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Requirements and component freeze | Indoor-first direction, fan/filter candidates, draft supplier questions, clean/loaded sensitivities | Actual test room/site, accepted flow/noise targets, exact purchasable fan/filter, OEM drawings/curves/orientation/masses, real quotes | Team + suppliers; assistant can compare documented responses |
| 2. Mechanical design release | Round packaging, cassette/frame branches, new independent housing fit, weight/load sensitivities | Pick architecture; resolve tight service margins; detail seals/doors/guards, fan mounts, frame/base/joints; full mass/CG, structural/stability checks; drawings and manufacturing BOM | Assistant prepares; paid qualified mechanical reviewer + fabricator, with OEM inputs |
| 3. Electrical/control release | Functional electrical plan and monitoring intent | Exact OEM power/control wiring, rated protection/isolation/earthing, enclosure/cable design, safety functions, inspection/commissioning plan | Qualified electrical reviewer/assembler; assistant can document verified design, not approve mains safety |
| 4. Procurement, build and commissioning | Preliminary BOM and test sequence | Confirm funding/quotes, order released parts, fabricate/assemble, inspect mechanically/electrically, verify guards/seals and safe operation | Team + vendors + qualified workshop staff |
| 5. Indoor physical validation | Digital airflow/particle evidence and proposed test plan | Measure actual airflow, filter/guard losses, installed bypass, PM reduction under controlled conditions, noise, power and maintenance behavior; report limitations | Safe controlled room, instruments, qualified supervision; assistant can analyze recorded data |
| 6. Outdoor pilot and scale-up | Outdoor goal and chain-of-local-zones concept | Site/weather/anchoring/public safety design; approved pilot; wind/background/nearby PM monitoring; establish any real benefit before tower spacing/network claims | Site permission + relevant reviewers + field testing |

**None of these gates is closed by a “no clash” CAD result or passing unit tests.** Digital testing is not a physical tower demonstration. A stakeholder presentation can explain current progress now, but must not call the design construction-ready or claim a proven outdoor bubble.

## What can move forward here without pretending missing facts exist

- Refine manufacturability/service envelopes, compare material/weight options and prepare reviewer-ready connection concepts.
- Maintain the full pressure budget and compare exact OEM duty data once supplied.
- Develop low-voltage data logging and instrument documentation separately from mains safety functions.
- Prepare a consolidated design-review package and update this checklist when actual evidence closes an item.

## Inputs needed from outside the CAD work

Obtain exact fan and filter drawings/curves/masses and confirm allowed orientation. Quote qualified mechanical/electrical review services; optional ENTC feedback is not a guaranteed resource or a substitute for required competence. No fixed budget ceiling or demonstration date has been given. Availability, reviewer turnaround and workshop capacity are UNKNOWN. We therefore cannot honestly promise a number of days/weeks or a completion percentage yet. More CAD branches cannot replace missing OEM data or engineering review.
